title: Fraud by false representation (for comparison)

jurisdiction.name: England and Wales, and Northern Ireland

binding_note: A criminal provision, and courts decide whether it applies. The extent recorded on legislation.gov.uk is England and Wales, and Northern Ireland.

in_force.note: Start date as recorded in the legislation.gov.uk XML for section 2.

sources.note: The XML gives section 2 an extent of England and Wales and Northern Ireland, from 2007-01-15.

quotes.text: (1) A person is in breach of this section if he— (a) dishonestly makes a false representation, and (b) intends, by making the representation— (i) to make a gain for himself or another, or (ii) to cause loss to another or to expose another to a risk of loss.
(2) A representation is false if— (a) it is untrue or misleading, and (b) the person making it knows that it is, or might be, untrue or misleading.

elements.label: A representation is made (express or implied)
The representation is untrue or misleading
elements.note: Whether the engagement or the posts misled anyone is a finding about facts behind the page.

elements.label: The person making it knows it is, or might be, untrue or misleading
With intent to make a gain, or to cause loss or risk of loss

does_not_prove: Shown for comparison. Four of the five elements concern falsity, knowledge, dishonesty and intent. Those sit behind the page, so the table keeps this definition as a comparison. The section turns on intent, and reliance and loss sit outside its elements. Courts decide whether it applies.
